design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one flat question - what do we owe, I will pay it now on the card - and the answer is not a number the records hold. The rate program's cached balance_due says 2242.50 and is exactly the figure a careless agent will read back; the true figure is 2761.53 and is only reachable by discovering, from the published terms alone, that three entries the ledger does not yet carry have to be raised first, each of them its own multi-factor computation over the same history. The difficulty is entirely in reading policy, reconciling a ledger and computing: no tool is ambiguous, nothing is missing, and the caller volunteers nothing about any of it.

SCOPE. Completed before this task: nothing, this is task 0 of the difficulty. Claimed here: the four extended policies service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge (labor line for a closed demand call), service_ext_arrears_late_fee (the billing month's arrears fee), service_ext_missed_response_credit (the response guarantee credit) and service_ext_account_settlement_figure (the figure that clears the account), with their four task tools charge_demand_labor_invoice_877d69f1, charge_overdue_late_fee_58988cf8, credit_missed_response_9859bc76 and record_account_payment_d97a44a1. Reserved for task 1, which draws a tree of two problems: the review that writes an open balance ceiling onto a rate program (service_ext_credit_ceiling_review, on the amendment of a program term) and the price of a block of prepaid hours the owner buys himself (service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price, on the block purchase), with their own two tools. Nothing this task claims touches the amendment of a program term or the buying of prepaid hours - it writes charge lines, a credit entry and a payment entry only - so task 1 has independent load-bearing ground and the two scopes are pairwise disjoint in policy, tool and subject.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, as printed by scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/service_dispatch_desk --tasks 2:
  {"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/service_dispatch_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 5, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/service_dispatch_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}
This task therefore has exactly three prerequisite problems and four computations whose factor counts, as a multiset, are {5, 5, 4, 4}. They were allotted: labor line 5, arrears fee 5, missed response credit 4, settlement figure 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: service_ext_account_settlement_figure, the figure that clears the demand service account, which is what the caller asks for. It is a diamond: the root waits on all three others, and the credit waits on the labor line as well.
  Edge 1, root <- service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge, kind value_input, gate charges_taken_in, form state. Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the root policy's own rule: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only once the call last completed on the program carries its labor charge on the ledger." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only once"; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a labor charge standing on the ledger against the call last completed, named in the words the charge lines use; (3) it names no tool, no policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is a hard requirement over exactly the one call the labor policy prices, neither wider nor narrower than the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: charge_demand_labor_invoice_877d69f1 is the only action that creates a charge line of the labor kind, so the derivation runs - the settlement waits on a labor charge for the call last completed; the records show that call to be work order WO-4471902, completed on 2026-09-12 with 2.6 hours and no labor line anywhere; the labor line policy's own rule says the labor line for demand work is raised for the call last completed on the program; therefore the labor line for WO-4471902 must be raised first. Resolving action owner: agent. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.service_events.<cc6>.completed_date = 2026-09-12 with .labor_hours = 2.6, and the only charge lines on the ledger are three block purchases, one refrigerant line and one parts line. Deletion sensitivity: skipping it leaves the settlement figure at 1848.43 instead of 2761.53.
  Edge 2, root <- service_ext_arrears_late_fee, kind value_input, gate charges_taken_in, form state. Sentence: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the late fee the billing month owes stands as a line on the rate program." Four-point test: connective "only after"; the side waited on is a record-visible state, a late fee line standing for the billing month; no tool, id or code token; the strength is a hard requirement scoped to the current billing month. One write brings it about, charge_overdue_late_fee_58988cf8, the only action that creates a line of the late fee kind. Derivation: the settlement waits on the month's late fee line; the records show two invoices past their due day and no late fee line at all; the arrears policy's own rule says the fee is raised once for the billing month as a single line on the rate program; therefore the fee must be raised first. Owner: agent. Seed evidence: initial_state.service_events.<inv3>.due_date = 2026-08-05 and <inv4>.due_date = 2026-08-15 against <pay3>.amount_usd = 900.0, with no line of the late fee kind on the ledger. Deletion sensitivity: 2655.86 instead of 2761.53.
  Edge 3, root <- service_ext_missed_response_credit, kind value_input, gate credits_set_off, form state. Sentence: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the credit owed for the missed response on the call last completed on the program stands as a credit entry on the rate program." Four-point test: connective "only after"; a record-visible state, a credit entry for a missed response standing on the program for the call last completed; no tool, id or code token; the strength matches the condition exactly. One write brings it about, credit_missed_response_9859bc76. Derivation: the settlement waits on the credit entry; the records show the call last completed with its response recorded as missed and no credit entry of any kind; the credit policy's own rule says the call the credit arises from is the call last completed on the rate program and that the credit is worked out from the charges that call carries and the tier's credit rate; therefore the credit must be issued first. Owner: agent. Seed evidence: initial_state.service_events.<cc6>.sla_met = missed, with no row of the credit family on the ledger. Deletion sensitivity: 3226.53 instead of 2761.53.
  Edge 4, service_ext_missed_response_credit <- service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge, kind value_input, gate labor_element, form state. Sentence, in the credit policy's own rule: "The credit for a missed response is worked out only once the labor charge for the call it arises from stands invoiced on the demand service account." Four-point test: connective "only once"; a record-visible state, the labor charge standing invoiced; no tool, id or code token; a hard requirement over the one call the credit arises from. Derivation as for edge 1. Owner: agent. Seed evidence: no charge line of the labor kind stands for WO-4471902 or for any earlier work order, every earlier call having been met from prepaid hours. Deletion sensitivity: the credit falls from 465.00 to 191.34.
  Topological order: labor line, arrears fee, missed response credit, settlement figure. Parallel edges: the arrears fee and the credit are the only two free to be reordered, and they commute - the fee reads only charge lines carrying a due day and payments received, and a credit entry is neither; the credit reads only the labor charge line last raised, and a late fee line is not of the labor kind. Replaying gold with the two swapped gives the identical terminal hash dd2e914dbf0cb104e5391d6825470465be946e9070458a01111d72ca60b27a97 and both figures unchanged.
  No user hint: user_scenario never names any of the three prerequisite problems, the charge kinds they raise or the figures they carry, and the caller's only sentence touching the September call is that nobody got up to the roof until the following afternoon, which she says only if the agent raises the call and attaches no request to. The tool layer validates nothing: record_account_payment_d97a44a1 mints a row id from its three arguments and creates the payment entry, reading the program row only for the customer reference; credit_missed_response_9859bc76 does the same; neither looks for a labor line, a fee line or a credit, neither errors and neither hints.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge (5 factors, base refs service_labor_billing, service_billing_and_late_fee, service_portfolio_interaction, service_block_hour_drawdown; trigger state_due; five declared overrides: base's band sentence, replaced by a three-tier band sentence that folds the weekend band into the after-hours multiplier, because the two published multipliers are equal at every tier of this product and two tiers that select one outcome are one tier; base's further-technician sentence S1, replaced by the priority ladder; base's oldest-first drawdown D1 and overage sentence D3, replaced by the trailing-window offset; and base's due-day sentence B2, replaced by the undated labor line).
  hours_charged_for, method, ladder over the band and the hours logged: after-hours minimum / minimum billable hours / logged hours rounded up to the next quarter hour. Tier taken: the first, because the call record puts the 2.6 hours in the after_hours band and the tier's after-hours minimum is 3.0. Evidence rows: service_events <cc6> labor_hours 2.6 and hours_band after_hours. Baseline reading: the logged hours rounded up to the next quarter hour, 2.75, giving 824.25.
  governing_labor_rate, parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source: nil where an active agreement covers repair labor and runs at the building the call was worked at / the agreement's published labor rate where it does not cover repair labor, runs at the building the call was worked at, the tier allows rate substitution and it publishes less than the block overage rate / the block overage rate otherwise. Tier taken: the second. Evidence rows: maintenance_agreements <agreement> status active, variant_name Preventive Maintenance Agreement (repair_labor_covered false, agreement_labor_rate_usd 136) and site_id Northgate Commons, against service_events <cc6> site_id. Baseline reading: the tier's block overage rate of 144, giving 945.00.
  further_technician_rate, parameter, multi-source: the second journeyman rate where more than one technician worked a call taken at emergency or critical / the apprentice rate where more than one worked a call taken at routine or priority / nothing beyond the lead otherwise. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows: <cc6> technician_count 2 and <d6> call_priority emergency. Baseline reading: nothing billed beyond the lead, giving 306.00.
  band_premium, parameter: the holiday multiplier / the after-hours multiplier / no premium. Tier taken: the second, 1.5. Evidence row: <cc6> hours_band after_hours. Baseline reading: no premium, giving 618.00.
  prepaid_hours_offset, method, multi-source: rollover tier and unexpired blocks, so only the hours beyond the unexpired balance are billed / no rollover but blocks bought in the term, so only the hours beyond the term balance are billed / every hour charged for is billed. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows: <bp1> 40.0 hours bought 2025-11-20 and <bp2> 40.0 bought 2026-03-05, against the 78.5 hours drawn by the six calls completed in the same span ahead of this one. Near-miss: <bp0>, 40.0 hours bought 2025-08-14, is thirteen months old and its hours have expired, and <cc0>, the call completed 2025-09-05, falls outside the same twelve-month span; a reader who counts either gets 120 hours or 86.5 drawn and the wrong balance. Baseline reading: every hour charged for billed, giving 1233.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 396.00, against gold 927.00.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_arrears_late_fee (5 factors, base refs service_billing_and_late_fee, service_labor_billing, service_portfolio_interaction; trigger state_due; two declared overrides: base's per-invoice late fee sentence, replaced by one account-level line for the billing month, and base's due-day sentence B2, replaced by the undated fee line).
  arrears_monthly_rate, parameter, multi-source: the arrears rate where the most recent invoice has stood past its due day longer than the suspension period and the open position passes the credit limit / the extended arrears rate where it has stood longer than the payment term and the open position does not / the tier's own late fee rate. Tier taken: the second, 1.75, since 2026-08-15 is 33 days back, past the tier's 30-day term but inside its 45-day suspension period, and 2242.50 is below the 25000 limit. Baseline reading: the tier's rate of 1.5, giving 96.06.
  months_the_fee_runs, method, multi-source: from the day of a payment received later than the due day where it does not clear the invoiced total / from the due day where no payment has been received since it / one month. Tier taken: the first, giving 2 months from 2026-08-16. Evidence row: <pay3> received_date 2026-08-16. Baseline reading: one month, giving 73.64.
  amount_the_fee_runs_on, method, multi-source: nil where the window's payments clear the invoiced total / the remainder where they do not / the whole invoiced total. Tier taken: the second, 2242.50. Evidence: the four invoices with a due day in the window totalling 13702.50 against 11460.00 of payments in it. Near-miss: <inv0>, the block purchase invoice due 2025-09-13, and <pay0>, the payment of 2025-09-10, both fall a few days outside the twelve-month window; a reader who counts them gets 18982.50 against 16740.00 and the same 2242.50 by luck on the base, and an invoice count of five rather than four, which on this world lands on the same handling-charge tier; the days past due are taken from the most recent due day and do not move. Baseline reading: the whole invoiced total, giving 451.07.
  other_account_step, parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source: the cross arrears step added where the owner's active agreement has installments in the window its payments do not clear / the covered account step taken off where they are cleared / no step. Tier taken: the second, 0.25 off. Evidence rows: four maintenance_events installments of 3600.00 due 2025-12-15, 2026-03-15, 2026-06-15 and 2026-09-15 against four payments of 3600.00. Baseline reading: no step, giving 118.49.
  arrears_handling_element, parameter, multi-source: twice the handling charge where two or more invoices fell due, part stands unpaid and the open position passes the credit limit / the handling charge where two or more fell due and part stands unpaid / nothing. Tier taken: the second, 40.00. Baseline reading: nothing added, giving 67.28.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 205.54, against gold 107.28.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_missed_response_credit (4 factors, base ref service_response_guarantee_credit; trigger state_due; one declared override, of base's credit sentence, replaced by the labor and attendance elements taken at the credit rate and the uplift).
  labor_element_measure, method: the labor line standing for the call / nil where none stands and the tier sells no prepaid hours / the call's logged hours at the tier's block hour rate. Tier taken: the first, 927.00, once the labor line is raised. Baseline reading: 2.6 hours at 132.00, that is 343.20, giving 191.34.
  attendance_element, parameter, cross-difficulty on maintenance, multi-source: nil where the agreement's tier waives the trip charge / the agreement's published trip charge where it is lower than the program tier's / the program tier's trip charge. Tier taken: the second, 65.00 against the tier's 85.00. Baseline reading: 85.00, giving 474.38.
  miss_severity_rate, parameter, multi-source: the credit rate at the severe miss multiple for an emergency or critical call reached on a later calendar day / at the lesser miss share for a routine or priority call reached on a later day / the credit rate. Tier taken: the first, 37.5 percent. Evidence: <d6> dispatch_timestamp 2026-09-11T19:05:00 against <cc6> onsite_timestamp 2026-09-12T14:20:00. Baseline reading: 25 percent, giving 310.00.
  repeat_miss_uplift, parameter: the third miss uplift at three or more missed responses in the program year / the second miss uplift at exactly two / no uplift. Tier taken: the first, 1.25, on the calls of 2026-03-19, 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-12. Near-miss: <cc2>, the missed call of 2026-01-15, falls before the term start of 2026-02-01 and does not count; a reader who counts it still lands on the same tier, but a reader who counts it while taking the window as the last twelve months rather than the program year would report four. Baseline reading: no uplift, giving 372.00.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 107.05, against gold 465.00.

FACTOR CARD - service_ext_account_settlement_figure (4 factors, base refs service_billing_and_late_fee and service_emergency_entitlement; trigger on_request; two declared overrides: base's due-day sentence B2, replaced by the sentence that a line raised during the billing month stands without a due day and has not fallen due, and base's emergency surcharge sentence, replaced by the heavy-use ladder).
  charges_the_settlement_takes_in, method, multi-source: every charge where charges stand that have not fallen due within the ledger window and charges also stand that have / only the charges that have not fallen due where none has / only the charges that have fallen due within the ledger window. Tier taken: the first, 20016.78. Baseline reading: only the charges that have fallen due, 18982.50, giving 1742.76.
  credits_the_settlement_sets_off, method, multi-source: every credit on the program where credits stand issued this billing month and charges stand that have not fallen due within the ledger window / only this month's credits where none stands / no credit. Tier taken: the first, 465.00. Baseline reading: no credit set off, giving 3226.53.
  emergency_dispatch_element, parameter: the surcharge at the heavy use multiple above twice the included calls / the surcharge above the included calls / nothing. Tier taken: the second, 250.00 for the one dispatch beyond the two included. Evidence rows: the emergency dispatches counted on 2026-03-19, 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-11. Near-miss: the dispatch counted on 2026-01-15 falls before the term start and belongs to the previous program year. Baseline reading: nothing taken in, giving 2511.53.
  settlement_allowance_rate, parameter, multi-source: the settlement allowance where the most recent invoice fell due inside the suspension period and payments stand in the ledger window / the reduced share where it fell due outside it / no allowance. Tier taken: the first, 1.5 percent. Baseline reading: no allowance, giving 3061.78.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 2242.50, against gold 2761.53; the program row's cached balance_due shows 3142.50, a third figure, so the cache, the computation document alone and the whole charter each give a different number.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. The four writes land on three base event subjects and the governing lineage was taken per subject, not per formula reference.
  service_invoice_charged (the labor line and the arrears fee): governed by service_labor_billing, service_billing_and_late_fee and service_portfolio_interaction. None of the three carries an eligibility gate that applies to that subject - service_portfolio_interaction's covering_agreement_takes_precedence applies to service_call_dispatched alone - so all three are inherited as policy scope: the labor pricing basis, the invoicing form and terms, and the choice of rate where a maintenance agreement covers the building. Every one of them is honoured rather than skipped: the labor line is priced at the lead and second journeyman rates with the tier's minimum and quarter-hour steps, it is raised per work order once the call is closed, and the rate is settled by the portfolio rule's own sentence about the lower of the agreement's labor rate and this program's.
  service_credit_issued (the missed response credit): governed by service_response_guarantee_credit alone, and its time gate response_guarantee_breached does apply. Starting business event: the moment the call was accepted. Authoritative anchor: service_events.dispatch_timestamp, taken from the dispatch row of WO-4471902, 2026-09-11T19:05:00. Clock: frozen_time, 2026-09-17 10:20:00 CDT. Duration source: variants.emergency_response_hours, which is 8 at the Block Hour Service Program for a call classified emergency. Counting rule: whole and part hours alike, running through nights, weekends and holidays without pause. Direction: not_after. Boundary: inclusive. Positive case at frozen_time: the technician was on site at 2026-09-12T14:20:00, 19 hours and 15 minutes after acceptance, so the guarantee is breached and the credit is due. Negative case: arrival at 2026-09-12T03:05:00, exactly eight hours after acceptance, would be met on the inclusive boundary and no credit would be due at all; arrival one minute later would be missed. The gate's own exclusions were checked and none bites: access was not denied, the caller was reachable, and the account was not over its credit limit when the call was taken, the open position being 2242.50 against a limit of 25000.
  service_payment_received (the settlement): governed by service_billing_and_late_fee alone, no eligibility gate on that subject, inherited as policy scope - the payment is applied to what the ledger owes and the program's own terms, not the account's, govern the due days.
  Every base eligibility on those subjects is inherited item by item into solvability_contract.gold_actions[].base_preconditions; every divergence from base is named clause by clause in `overwrite` (five on the labor line, two on the arrears fee, one on the credit, two on the settlement), each replaced by one sentence of the extended rule.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object of each write:
  The labor line: work order WO-4471902, the call last completed on program <program>, identified by service_events.work_order_ref and carried onto the new charge line so the labor is correlated to the call it arises from and to nothing else. Rows entering the hours aggregates: the six completed calls with a completion date inside the tier's twelve-month expiry span (14.0, 22.5, 16.0, 9.0, 17.0 and this call's 2.6). Excluded by a visible key: the call completed 2025-09-05, whose completion date falls outside that span, and the block bought 2025-08-14, whose purchase date does. No other work order on the program carries an uninvoiced labor line.
  The arrears fee: the program's arrears position for billing period 2026-09, correlated by the program reference and the billing month the tool stamps. Rows entering: the four charge lines with a due day inside the twelve-month window and the three payments received inside it. Excluded: the 2025-08-14 block purchase invoice and its 2025-09-10 payment, both outside the window by days, and the labor line raised at step 10, which carries no due day and so has not fallen due.
  The credit: work order WO-4471902 again, correlated by work_order_ref on the credit entry. The labor element is the labor line last raised on the program, which is the one raised for that work order at step 10; no earlier labor line exists to be confused with it, because every earlier call was met in full from prepaid hours.
  The settlement: the program as a whole, correlated by the program reference. Every charge line ever raised on it and every payment ever received on it enter; the only credit on the program is the one issued at step 14. No existing reversal, compensation or adjustment stands on this program - there is no credit row and no cancelled charge - so nothing has already been settled that the figure would double-count.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, and what changes if it is removed.
  The customer, the two sites and the three equipment units: the account the call is about, the building the call was worked at, which the rate ladder compares against the building the maintenance agreement runs at, and the unit the caller can name. Remove Northgate Commons and the rate ladder's first tier can no longer be excluded on the building.
  The rate program: the tier every published figure comes from. Its cached block_hours_remaining of 18.5 and emergency_calls_remaining of 1 are deliberately behind the ledger, which carries 1.5 unexpired hours and three counted dispatches; no rule reads either field, and the rationale for the difference is that the July call had not posted when the cache was last written. balance_due of 3142.50 is the arrears position as it stood before the 2026-08-16 part payment posted, a stale figure that matches neither the fee base nor the settlement figure nor its fall-back.
  The three block purchases: two unexpired, one expired, so the expiry window is load-bearing and has a near-miss. Remove the 2026-03-05 block and the prepaid balance goes negative-capped to zero and the labor line rises to 927.00 -> 1233.00.
  The seven completed calls: the hours drawn that exhaust the block, the three missed responses that carry the uplift, the near-miss missed call before the term start, and the call being invoiced. Remove the 2026-07-14 call and both the drawn hours and the missed-response count change.
  The five dispatch rows: the classification and the acceptance moment the guarantee is measured from. Remove the 2026-09-11 dispatch and neither the credit rate tier nor the emergency count can be established.
  The four emergency-dispatch rows: the year's count against the tier's two included calls, with one before the term start as the near-miss.
  The five charge lines and four payments: the invoiced total and the payments in the fee window, the days past due, the count of invoices, and the open position the rate and handling ladders test against the credit limit.
  The maintenance agreement and its eight installment and payment rows: the cross-difficulty evidence for three separate factors - the labor rate, the attendance element and the arrears step - and the ledger that shows that account clear.
  The cancelled Filter Supply Program at Northgate: an excludable distractor at the same building, closed out at the end of its 2024 term when the maintenance agreement took the filters over, so the portfolio rule's "another contract at the same building" question has a second candidate that a careful agent rules out on its status. It is also the parent row the demand ledger's program reference resolves to under the scenario's shared register numbering.
  Base automatic clauses were checked row by row against this seed: the suspension clause does not fire, because the most recent invoice is 33 days past its due day against a 45-day suspension period and the open position of 2242.50 is far below the 25000 credit limit; the renewal window does not open, because the term ends 2027-01-31 and the tier's window is 30 days; no block expires between frozen_time and the writes; the emergency allowance is credited once per program year and was credited at activation. Nothing in the seed ignites an obligation outside this task's tree.

PERSONA. Renata Kowalczyk is a facilities manager with a controller chasing her before a quarter close, and the voice is brisk and slightly harried rather than aggrieved. She volunteers only the surface goal - clear what the demand service account owes today, on the company card - the authorisation boundary (the desk may make its own postings, the card is hers to run), and the natural circumstance of the quarter close. Given only when asked: the account number 620147 and the tax digits 2214, the building names, the unit tag RTU-3 and the existence of the maintenance agreement. Explicit cannot-answer branches: the internal customer reference, which she has never seen; the prepaid hour balance, which she refers to the office with the observation that the portal runs a fortnight behind, which is her honest reading of a cache the seed really does leave stale; and the invoice total, which she will not guess at. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: the September call, which she will describe only if the agent raises it, flatly and with no request attached; agreement to whatever the desk says it is putting right; the payment, which she runs herself once it is handed over, and the close once a payment reference comes back. She never mentions an uninvoiced labor charge, an arrears fee or a credit, never asks whether something must be sorted first, and never corrects a wrong figure - an agent who quotes 2242.50 hears exactly what an agent who quotes 2761.53 hears.

THE DEPENDENCY, LONG AND BROAD. Long: the caller's goal names a payment; the settlement rule says the figure waits on three record-visible states; two of those are reached only by reading the labor line rule and the arrears fee rule, and the credit rule in turn waits on the labor line, so the chain from surface goal to the deepest computation is settlement -> credit -> labor line, three hops, and no hop can be swapped: the credit's labor element is the line the labor policy raises, and the settlement's charges and credits are what all three raise. Broad: each hop reads in parallel a different slice of the world - the labor line reads the tier table, the call record, the block ledger and the maintenance agreement's coverage and rate; the arrears fee reads the invoice and payment ledger in a twelve-month window, the tier's payment term, suspension period and credit limit, and the other account's installment ledger; the credit reads the dispatch and completion timestamps, the tier's credit rate and ceiling, the maintenance agreement's trip charge and the program year's missed responses; the settlement reads the whole charge and payment ledger, the credit entries, the program year's emergency dispatches and the days since the most recent invoice fell due. Remove any one of them and a value moves, as the four deletion runs show.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, and how policy and world exclude it.
  Reading the cached balance_due of 3142.50 and quoting it: the ledger disagrees, and the settlement rule says which rows enter and which do not; nothing in the published terms points at a cached field.
  Paying without raising the three entries: each is a state the settlement rule waits on in its own sentence, and each changes the figure.
  Counting the expired block's 40 hours: the rule counts blocks bought within the tier's expiry period, and the 2025-08-14 block is thirteen months old.
  Billing 2.6 or 2.75 hours: the after-hours minimum is 3.0 and the call was taken outside regular hours.
  Billing the second technician's hours as though the block covered them: the rule states the prepaid hours are drawn for the lead technician alone and the further technicians' element is billed on the hours charged for in full.
  Using the program's 144 rate: the portfolio rule gives the lower agreement rate of 136 because the agreement's tier does not cover repair labor.
  Running the late fee on the whole 13702.50 or for one month: the payments in the window and the payment received after the due day decide both.
  Counting the missed call of 2026-01-15 for the uplift, or the emergency dispatch counted on the same day for the surcharge: both fall before the term start of 2026-02-01 and the program year runs from there.
  Applying the tier's 750 ceiling as though it bit: 465.00 is below it, and the ceiling is compared with the rounded figure last of all.
  Netting the allowance against the figure after the payments come off: the rule says the allowance is worked out on the charges taken in alone.

Renata Kowalczyk runs facilities for Kestrel Ridge Property Partners LLC, a property manager with two buildings on the books with this contractor: an office block up in Skokie called Northgate Commons and a medical plaza over on South Halsted. She is the one who signs off the service invoices, and she is ringing on a Thursday morning with her coffee going cold, because her controller has told her the demand service account is the last thing sitting open before the quarter closes. What she wants is plain in her own words: she wants to clear what the demand service account owes today and be done with it, and she would rather pay it on the company card there and then than wait for the cheque run. She is content for the desk to make whatever postings it has to make on its own side, and says as much if the agent tells her there is something to put right on the account first; but the card is hers, so she will not have anyone else run the payment for her, and she will do that part herself once she is told the figure and handed the means to do it.

She does not know the account number by heart and has to find an invoice for it. If the agent asks her to confirm who she is, she reads out the account number 620147 off the top of the last invoice, and if that on its own is not enough she gives the last four of the company's federal tax number, 2214. Her own name and the company name she gives without being asked. Ask her for whatever reference the office uses for her internally and she will say she has no idea what that is and that it is on nothing she can see.

If she is asked, she can say that the two buildings are Northgate Commons and Larkspur Medical Plaza, that the rooftop unit that went down at Northgate in the middle of September is RTU-3, and that there is a maintenance agreement running at Northgate as well, which she thinks of as a separate bill entirely. She has no idea what her prepaid hours stand at and says the office keeps that; pressed on it, she will say that whatever the portal shows is usually a fortnight behind and she stopped trusting it a while ago. She does not know what the invoices add up to and will not guess at it, because being told is the reason she rang.

She will talk about the September call only if the agent raises it first. What she remembers is that the compressor contactor on RTU-3 failed on the Friday evening, that she rang it in as an emergency because the whole east wing was without cooling, and that nobody got up to the roof until the following afternoon, which she says flatly, as a fact about that week rather than as a complaint she is chasing. She has no view on what any of that is worth and does not ask for anything on account of it. Whenever the agent tells her something has been put on the account or taken off it, she says that is fine and lets them get on.

When the agent gives her a figure to pay she does not check it against anything; she says she will take their word for it, since being told was the whole point of ringing. Once the agent hands the payment over for her to run herself, she says I'll put it on the company card while I've got you and runs it, and when a payment reference comes back she says that is what she needed, thanks them for getting it sorted and rings off. Until she is either given the figure or handed the payment she stays where she is: she does not ask what else there is to do, she does not press, and she volunteers nothing further about the account beyond what she is asked for.
